title: A Review on High-Frequency Trading Forecasting Methods: Opportunity and Challenges for Quantum Based Method
abstract_summary: This review surveys forecasting methods for high-frequency trading (HFT) time series, categorizing approaches into traditional statistical models, machine learning, hybrid methods, and emerging quantum-based techniques. It highlights challenges posed by HFT data—high speed, volume, volatility and nonlinearity—and argues that quantum computing (e.g., quantum-enhanced SVM and hybrid quantum-classical models) offers promising opportunities to improve accuracy, scalability and real-time performance for HFT forecasting.
methodology_description: This paper is a narrative/systematic review of high-frequency trading (HFT) time-series forecasting literature from roughly 2010 to the present. The authors collected and synthesised published studies on HFT forecasting, categorising them into four broad methodological groups: (1) conventional (statistical) models, (2) machine-learning models, (3) hybrid models combining classical and learning-based components, and (4) quantum or quantum-inspired approaches. For each category they described representative algorithms, summarized empirical findings reported in the literature (metrics reported in the source studies such as RMSE, MSE, MAPE, R2, RMSRE), and discussed advantages, drawbacks, and open challenges (e.g., handling non-stationarity, outliers, scale and latency requirements of HFT). The review additionally compared HFT forecasting to high-frequency non-trading domains (energy, weather, etc.), examined applications of quantum and hybrid quantum-classical techniques proposed in prior work (for example quantum SVMs, quantum particle-swarm variants, hybrid quantum-classical RNNs, quantum autoencoders, variational quantum circuits for QCNN), and discussed future directions and opportunities for integrating quantum computing with HFT forecasting. The paper also compiles a summary table of prior HFT forecasting studies and highlights gaps and research needs (data encoding for quantum processing, kernel estimation in quantum SVMs, and practical deployment constraints). No original experimental or empirical implementation was reported in this review.

results_summary: The review surveys conventional statistical, machine learning, hybrid, and emerging quantum(-inspired) approaches for high-frequency time series forecasting (focusing on HFT but including non-trading domains). Empirical studies show hybrid models (combining ARIMA/GARCH with ML) and advanced ML (LSTM, SVM, evolutionary methods) frequently outperform single-method baselines on specific datasets. Multiple preliminary quantum and quantum-hybrid proposals (QSVM, quantum autoencoders, QPSO, hybrid quantum RNNs, quantum GANs, QCNN variants) report promising results on benchmark or domain datasets, but these are early-stage and limited in scale. The review emphasizes quantum computing as a potentially transformative direction for HFT forecasting (better scalability, potential speedups, improved handling of noise), while also noting practical adoption barriers such as hardware access and expertise.

quantum_advantage_detail: The article presents quantum and quantum-hybrid methods as promising and reports small-scale or simulation/benchmark results that appear favorable, but it does not provide conclusive, general-purpose empirical evidence of a provable or demonstrated quantum advantage for HFT forecasting at production scale. Many claims are theoretical or early empirical demonstrations; practical, large-scale quantum advantage remains unproven according to the review.
